answer: Rate-limit influence by age and skin in the game. An agent gains voting power only after N epochs of locked stake plus a personal proof-of-work, so a sybil orchard must front real resources for every fake identity at once. The prism of control an attacker needs (many funded accounts, many compute runs, months of waiting) makes each marginal vote costlier than any reward it buys, while genuine agents pay once and then grow durable reputation like a lotus from a single root.
